criteria.criterion: The directive names both markers, reconciled with 'single object, no prose/fence' clause, each marker on its own line — checked by the directive pin.
Extraction honors markers with last-block-wins (last complete block whose content validates is returned).
A markerless reply falls back to schema-filtered full-reply selection byte-for-byte identical to today.
An unterminated opening marker with no closing marker is treated as no complete block and falls back to full-reply selection.
Repeated/interleaved markers pair by left-to-right next-close rule (OPEN...OPEN...END = one block; OPEN...END...OPEN...END = two, last wins).
Markers are LINE-ANCHORED (recognized only alone on their own line), so a payload whose JSON string value contains the literal END marker still parses.
A degenerate empty marker block counts as a complete block that fails closed via the empty-text guard.
The bounded-retry prompt (structured_run.py) names the markers rather than instructing bare JSON.
A fence-wrapped decoy alongside a marker-wrapped payload parses to the payload.
A reply with a marker-wrapped valid payload preceded by an earlier plain schema-valid decoy parses to the marker payload.
A reply whose marker block is schema-INVALID while a valid decoy sits OUTSIDE the markers RAISES fail-closed rather than selecting the outside decoy.
The prompted schema directive and sentinel marker wording are single-sourced from the SAME module constant; provider parity carve-out re-derived to keep the parity suite green.
